name: io.ballotwatch/congress
title: BallotWatch
description: U.S. Congress record: who represents you, how members voted, bills, floor schedule. Cited.

tools.name: find_representatives
tools.description: Resolve a U.S. street address or ZIP code to its two senators and House member, sitting members only. An address resolves to one exact district. A ZIP code that spans districts returns each district holding 1% or more of its land (location.districts) and the member for each; a district holding less is named in location.minor_overlaps without its members. Ask for a street address when the answer must be exact.

tools.name: search_members
tools.description: Find members of Congress by name, or list them by state, chamber or party. Use this first to turn a name such as "Chuck Schumer" or "AOC" into the Bioguide ID the other tools need. Nicknames, close spellings, titles ("Rep.", "Sen.") and a seat hint such as "(R-TX)" are understood. A name search also returns members who left during this Congress, marked serving: false; a list without a name shows sitting members only unless include_former is true.

query.description: Full or partial name, e.g. "Pelosi" or "Sen. Ted Cruz". Omit to list by the filters.

state.description: State or territory, by name or two-letter code, e.g. "Ohio" or "OH"

party.description: D, R or I (or Democrat, Republican, Independent)

include_former.description: Also list members who left during this Congress when no name is given

tools.name: get_member
tools.description: A member of Congress by Bioguide ID: seat, party, whether they are serving now, terms, vote statistics, and their ten latest votes.

tools.name: get_member_record
tools.description: A member's record in 60 seconds: seat, serving since, roll calls and votes cast / not voting this Congress, and the ten most recent votes with position and a link to each roll call. Use for a quick, neutral summary of how a member votes. Cite the record canonical URL and each vote's source_url.

tools.name: get_member_votes
tools.description: Recorded votes for a member, newest first, with the question, bill, position, and official source. Pass bill to answer "how did this member vote on H.R. 1" (every roll call on that bill), position to list only their Nay or Not Voting votes, and since / until for a date range. Page with offset.

bill.description: Only votes on this bill: 119-hr-1 or "H.R. 1"

position.description: Vote position, exactly one of "Yea", "Nay", "Present" or "Not Voting" (case-sensitive)

offset.description: Skip this many votes (for the next page)

tools.name: get_member_bills
tools.description: Bills a member sponsored (the newest 20) and cosponsored (the newest 10), with totals. The lists can be incomplete; each result links the member's full list on Congress.gov.

tools.name: compare_members
tools.description: How often two members of the same chamber voted the same way this Congress: the roll calls both voted Yea or Nay on, how many matched, and their ten most recent differing votes. A plain count over the whole record, not a score.

bioguide_id_a.description: Bioguide ID of the first member, e.g. P000197

bioguide_id_b.description: Bioguide ID of the second member, in the same chamber as bioguide_id_a, e.g. S000148

tools.name: get_recent_votes
tools.description: Roll-call votes, newest first, with the question, bill, tally and derived result. Use for "what did Congress vote on this week" or to find a roll call before calling get_roll_call, which adds the party split and how each member voted. Filter by chamber, date range, bill, or words in the question, description or bill title (query "nomination", "appropriations"). A bill number in query ("H.R. 1") is treated as that bill.

bill.description: Only roll calls on this bill: 119-hr-1 or "H.R. 1"

query.description: Words that must all appear in the question, description or bill title, and/or a bill number

tools.name: get_roll_call
tools.description: One roll-call vote: the question, bill, tally, party split, derived result, and how members voted. When more than 60 members match, they come back as short strings grouped by position; filter by state, party, position or bioguide_ids down to 60 or fewer (or pass format "full") to get one object per member, e.g. bioguide_ids to see how specific members voted or party "R" with position "Nay" for who broke ranks. result_derived is null when the record cannot decide it, such as a tied Senate vote the Vice President may have broken.

congress.description: Congress number, 1 to 200, e.g. 119 for the 119th Congress (2025-2026)

session.description: Session of that Congress, 1 to 3: normally 1 (first year) or 2 (second year), e.g. 1 for 2025 in the 119th Congress

roll.description: Roll-call number within that chamber and session, 1 to 5000, e.g. 145. get_recent_votes lists them.

state.description: State or territory, by name or two-letter code, e.g. "Ohio" or "OH"

party.description: D, R or I (or Democrat, Republican, Independent)

position.description: Vote position, exactly one of "Yea", "Nay", "Present" or "Not Voting" (case-sensitive)

format.description: "full" forces one object per member; "compact" forces grouped strings. Default: full for 60 members or fewer.

tools.name: search_bills
tools.description: Search bills by words in the title (every word must appear) or by bill number (e.g. "H.R. 1", "119-s-5051"), most recently introduced first. Narrow with congress, stage (e.g. enacted), sponsor (a Bioguide ID) or has_vote for bills that reached a recorded floor vote.

query.description: Title words or a bill number. Optional when another filter is given.

stage.description: Legislative stage, one of introduced, referred, subcommittee, committee, floor, passed_one, passed_both, enacted, dead (passed_one: passed one chamber; passed_both: passed both), e.g. "enacted"

has_vote.description: Only bills with a recorded floor vote

tools.name: get_bill
tools.description: A bill with sponsor, stage, official CRS summary, and every recorded floor vote.

tools.name: explain_bill
tools.description: A plain-English explanation of a bill for readers with no background in government: a one-sentence summary, short paragraphs and key points, written by AI from the bill's official text (or the CRS summary when the text is not published). Says which text version it read. Nothing is inferred from the title; when Congress.gov has no text yet, plain_english is null.

id.description: Bill id such as 119-hr-1, or a bill number such as "H.R. 1"

tools.name: get_floor_schedule
tools.description: What the House may take up this week and next (or the week containing a given date), read live from the Majority Leader's schedule on docs.house.gov: each item's label, title, procedure, and bill page. Use for "what is Congress voting on this week". House only; the Senate publishes no equivalent. Cite each week's source_url.

week.description: YYYY-MM-DD, any day of the week (normally the Monday). Omit for this week and next.

tools.name: search
tools.description: One search across members, bills and roll-call votes: a name, a ZIP code, a bill number, a roll call ("House roll call 327"), or words from a bill title or vote. Returns results as { id, title, url } for fetch. When you know what you are looking for, the specific tools (search_members, search_bills, get_recent_votes, find_representatives) give more detail and filters.

tools.name: fetch
tools.description: The full text of one record from search, as Markdown with its sources: a member's record (seat, votes cast this Congress, ten most recent votes), a bill (plain-English explanation, official summary, recorded votes), or a roll call (question, tally, party split and how every member voted). Takes an id from search (member:P000197, bill:119-hr-1, vote:house-119-1-145) or a ballotwatch.io record URL. Returns { id, title, text, url, metadata } as JSON.

id.description: An id returned by search, or a ballotwatch.io record URL
